Information since August points to robust real activity and a tight labor market, with inflation near the 2% objective and expectations little changed. The 25 bp hike to 2–2.25% and guidance for “further gradual increases” are consistent with a Taylor-rule style reaction function that satisfies the Taylor principle, as in the monetary policy rule literature (e.g., Taylor-type behavior; Lubik and Schorfheide’s empirical estimates). Emphasizing a symmetric 2% target and anchored expectations aligns with sticky-information and expectations-formation frameworks (Mankiw and Reis), and supports credibility in time-consistency models (Barro-Gordon; Goodfriend; Walsh). Given labor-market frictions and the imperfect link between unemployment and inflation (Ravenna and Walsh; Blanchard and Galí), gradualism is justified despite low unemployment. Orphanides’ real-time data caution further supports the Committee’s “risks roughly balanced” language to avoid over-tightening based on mismeasured slack. Overall tone: constructive growth with a mildly hawkish policy stance.
